name: Recapture of Constantinople
summary: On July 25, 1261, the Byzantine general Alexios Strategopoulos leads a small force across the Bosphorus and enters Constantinople through an unguarded gate while the main Latin garrison is absent on an expedition. He captures the city without a siege; Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos, who arranged this through the Treaty of Nymphaion (1261) with Genoa, enters the city in triumph. The Latin Empire of Constantinople ends after 57 years; the Byzantine Empire is formally restored and Michael crowns himself in Hagia Sophia.

_quarry.structural_significance: Ends the Latin Empire of Constantinople; restores Byzantine rule; drives Venice from its privileged position and replaces it with Genoa; but the restored Byzantine Empire lacks the strength of its predecessor
